question: Which three disciplines are integrated within the field of nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Nursing practice, business management, and engineering
options.D: Information technology, public health, and sociology

explanation: Nursing informatics integrates nursing science, computer science, and information science to manage and communicate data, information, knowledge, and wisdom. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is considered the primary purpose of health records within interprofessional healthcare teams?

options.A: Serving strictly as legal protection against malpractice lawsuits
options.B: Acting as the primary communication tool to share a unified view of patient status
options.C: Providing raw statistical data exclusively for government budgeting
options.D: Replacing verbal shift handovers entirely without exception

explanation: Health records serve as the primary communication tool among interprofessional healthcare teams, ensuring everyone shares a unified view of the patient's health status. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is a primary characteristic that distinguishes an Electronic Health Record (EHR) from a basic digitized document?

options.A: It can only be viewed by physicians within a single department.
options.B: It is designed to travel and be shared securely across different healthcare settings.
options.C: It is strictly limited to recording billing and financial transactions.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any physical nursing assessments.

explanation: An EHR is designed to be shared across different healthcare settings, departments, and hospitals to provide seamless continuity of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes the core concept of an EHR?

options.A: A real-time, patient-centered record accessible to authorized users
options.B: A static archive of handwritten shift reports stored in a basement
options.C: An open database accessible publicly on the internet without security
options.D: A tool used exclusively by hospital administrators for staffing schedules

explanation: The core concept of an EHR is a real-time, patient-centered record that makes information instantly and securely available to authorized users. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What was a major vulnerability of traditional paper-based health record systems in clinical settings?

options.A: They updated themselves automatically without human input.
options.B: They were prone to physical degradation, misplacement, and restricted simultaneous access.
options.C: They completely prevented any form of medical error.
options.D: They required continuous electricity and internet connectivity to function.

explanation: Paper files were prone to physical damage, getting lost, illegible handwriting, and could only be used by one person at a time. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do modern electronic health systems improve upon early digital systems that merely mimicked paper layouts?

options.A: By completely removing the need for nurses to document patient care
options.B: By incorporating clinical decision support tools and automated alerts for abnormal values
options.C: By making patient health data publicly accessible to anyone on social media
options.D: By ensuring that records can only be printed out and never viewed on screens

explanation: Modern EHRs incorporate advanced features like clinical decision support tools and automated alerts for abnormal laboratory values, enhancing patient safety. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical function of a Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE) and eMAR system?

options.A: Managing hospital utility bills and electricity generation
options.B: Reducing medication administration errors and tracking medication orders digitally
options.C: Printing physical flyers for health promotion campaigns
options.D: Tracking employee attendance and monthly salary disbursements

explanation: Systems like CPOE and eMAR help reduce medication administration errors by securely digitizing orders and matching them with patient identification. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: What purpose do system audit trails serve within an EHR platform?

options.A: They automatically delete old patient records after twenty-four hours.
options.B: They track every user interaction to ensure accountability and transparency in charting.
options.C: They restrict patients from ever viewing their own medical history.
options.D: They serve as a backup generator when hospital power fails.

explanation: Audit trails record every time a user accesses or modifies a file, ensuring accountability, transparency, and security. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following best describes an Electronic Medical Record (EMR)?

options.A: A nationwide database accessible by all hospitals in Nigeria simultaneously
options.B: The digital equivalent of a paper chart restricted primarily to a single facility or practice
options.C: An open public forum for patients to discuss their diagnoses online
options.D: A paper-only binder kept at the bedside for nursing care plans

explanation: An EMR is the digital version of a paper chart within a single facility and generally lacks broad external interoperability. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is a key advantage of an EHR over an EMR regarding patient data?

options.A: An EHR provides a holistic, longitudinal view of health data gathered from multiple providers and settings.
options.B: An EHR can only be edited by administrative clerks, keeping nurses from charting.
options.C: An EHR requires physical paper backup for every single digital entry made.
options.D: An EHR is exclusively used for billing and has no clinical information.

explanation: An EHR encapsulates clinical data from multiple healthcare settings over a lifetime, offering a comprehensive and longitudinal view of patient health. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: How do EHR safety features help prevent adverse drug events at the bedside?

options.A: By automatically administering intravenous medications without nurse supervision
options.B: By flagging documented patient allergies and potential drug-drug interactions before administration
options.C: By locking the medication cart whenever a doctor is absent
options.D: By prohibiting nurses from reviewing physician orders

explanation: Built-in safety alerts flag drug allergies and interactions, helping clinicians prevent adverse drug events before medication is given. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is one major way EHRs improve clinical workflow efficiency for nursing staff?

options.A: By allowing concurrent access to records, eliminating waiting times for physical charts
options.B: By removing all charting requirements from the nursing scope of practice
options.C: By replacing all direct patient communication with automated messaging
options.D: By guaranteeing that night shifts require zero documentation

explanation: Concurrent access allows multiple team members to view and update records at the same time, avoiding delays associated with waiting for physical charts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following represents a major infrastructural barrier to EHR implementation in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: An overabundance of high-speed internet in rural clinics
options.B: Unstable power supply and unreliable internet connectivity
options.C: Excessive willingness of staff to adopt new digital tools
options.D: Mandatory federal laws banning computers in hospital wards

explanation: Unstable power supply and unreliable internet connectivity are primary infrastructural challenges facing EHR deployment in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: How can resistance to change among healthcare personnel accustomed to paper records be addressed during EHR adoption?

options.A: By punishing staff who ask questions about computers
options.B: Through structured training programs and education in health informatics
options.C: By forcing staff to work without any software instruction
options.D: By reverting permanently to paper-only records

explanation: Providing structured training programs and education helps overcome digital illiteracy and resistance among staff accustomed to paper methods. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the purpose of role-based access control in an EHR system?

options.A: To allow any hospital visitor to view any patient chart freely
options.B: To ensure staff members only access records relevant to their assigned clinical duties
options.C: To automatically grade student nursing clinical performance logs
options.D: To prevent physicians from ever ordering laboratory tests

explanation: Role-based access control restricts system access so that users, such as nurses, only view data pertinent to their specific roles and patients. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Which best differentiates patient privacy from professional confidentiality in digital health?

options.A: Privacy is the patient's right to control personal info, while confidentiality is the nurse's duty to safeguard it.
options.B: Privacy only applies to paper records, while confidentiality applies to digital computers.
options.C: Privacy is a legal requirement for doctors, whereas confidentiality is optional for nurses.
options.D: Privacy refers to hospital building security guards, while confidentiality refers to IT passwords.

explanation: Privacy centers on the patient's right over their information, while confidentiality represents the healthcare provider's ethical duty to protect it. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is accurate and timely nursing documentation within an EHR vital?

options.A: It allows nurses to finish their shift early without providing patient handovers.
options.B: It ensures that nursing interventions, vital signs, and patient responses are logged precisely for safe care continuity.
options.C: It is used solely by billing departments to calculate hospital revenue.
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal communication among the healthcare team entirely.

explanation: Accurate and timely documentation ensures that vital patient care details are recorded precisely, supporting safe care continuity across shifts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)

question: In what way do nurses act as patient advocates within digital health ecosystems?

options.A: By blocking patients from ever seeing their own medical laboratory results
options.B: By safeguarding data privacy, educating patients on portal use, and communicating workflow bottlenecks
options.C: By taking over the role of hospital IT technicians and repairing broken computer hardware
options.D: By refusing to use electronic health records under any circumstances

explanation: Nurses advocate for patients by protecting data privacy, helping patients navigate portals, and reporting system issues that affect care quality. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)
